findings.text: Serial port descriptor centers on a spin lock plus port and memory access bases with shift and access style, clock and FIFO sizing, interrupt identity and flags, line and minor indices, mapping range, physical and core device links, human readable name and attribute groups. It carries pluggable register, modem, divisor, trigger, startup, shutdown, throttle, break, interrupt, power and protocol hooks, receive masks, link to parent state, counters, optional console link, flow and modem state, frame timing, type tag, operations table, divisor overrides, system request fields, suspend markers, serial bus and smart card settings with termination and direction controls, and an opaque platform pointer. Key links are known as ops, state and cons.

Port option bits below the user boundary mirror userspace serial flags while higher bits are core private. Only bits inside the change set may be altered from userspace, with speed selection and low latency forming a narrower user set. The build asserts equivalence between the change set and the userspace visible set. The change set travels under UPF_CHANGE_MASK while the narrower user set travels under UPF_USR_MASK. The internal quirk word holds UPQ_NO_TXEN_TEST for suppressing transmit enable probing.

Status word uses single bit positions zero through five for CTS enable, DCD enable, automatic RTS, automatic CTS, automatic XOFF and FIFO synchronization. Examples are UPSTAT_CTS_ENABLE at the low end and UPSTAT_SYNC_FIFO at the high end.

General option and internal quirk words require the port mutex for updates. Status word mutation requires termios semaphore plus port mutex plus port spin lock together, while a read may use any one of them.

Nonblocking port acquisition first attempts the port spin lock or its interrupt saving variant, then attempts nonblocking console acquisition when the port backs such a console; ports without that console mode succeed after the spin step. Failure at the second step releases the spin lock, restoring interrupt state in the saving variant, and reports failure. The console step alone unconditionally succeeds for non console ports.
Single register read helper delegates to the per port input hook with the supplied offset and returns its result.

Power tracking has three named conditions: fully on at zero, fully off at three for firmware compatibility, and an undefined transient. The condition lives in the parent state object rather than the port itself.

Parent state bundles an embedded TTY port, the power condition, an atomic reference count, a removal wait queue and a back link to the hardware port. Transmit buffering capacity equals one memory page.
Transmit wakeup threshold is two hundred fifty six characters of remaining buffered data.

Two helpers move outbound data from the TTY transmit queue while advancing the transmitted counter: one drains a bounded block into a caller buffer, the other retrieves a single byte. Both resolve the queue through the port back linked parent state.

Driver template holds module owner, driver and device name strings, major and minor bases, instance count and default console pointer as public configuration. Runtime state array and TTY driver pointer are core private and must start null, untouched by low level drivers.

Shared transmit pump gives priority to a pending high priority character, clearing it after emission, then stops if software flow control has halted output, then ends when the transmit queue is empty. Each emitted byte runs a caller supplied output action and advances the transmitted count, bounded either by an explicit countdown or run until a readiness test fails. After the loop a caller supplied completion action runs, remaining depth is measured, a write wakeup fires when below the wake threshold, and the queue empty case invokes the stop transmit hook unless UART_TX_NOSTOP is set.

Early console device pairs a console pointer with an embedded port, a short option string such as rate and framing, and a numeric baud rate. Its identifier carries a short name with explicit terminator, a longer compatibility string and a setup callback receiving the device and option text.

Build exposes early console registration through table placed identifiers and setup callbacks, allowing board and firmware code to publish a named early port before full console initialization. Records land in a dedicated aligned early table, either with explicit compatibility text or with an empty string, with retention annotation varying by configuration. When early support is disabled, setup becomes a trivial success stub and the firmware table enable flag is a constant.

Console registration test requires both a console association and a locked registration check. CTS handling distinguishes plain enablement from a software only mode where enablement is present without automatic CTS. Console hardware flow is reported active only when the port backs a console, RS485 mode is off, user console flow permission is set and CTS enablement holds.
System request input window spans five seconds measured in timer ticks.

Enabled build accepts a second character only when nonzero and arriving before the stored deadline: when the global mask permits it dispatches immediately and clears the deadline, otherwise it offers the character to a toggle helper and treats acceptance as consumed. Any other case clears the deadline and reports no action. Disabled build always reports no action.

Interrupt restoring release with deferred system request dispatch snapshots and clears the pending character while holding the port lock when that feature is present, releases the lock, then dispatches outside the lock if a character was pending. Ports without the feature, and the disabled build, simply release the lock.
Unix98 pseudoterminal limits are four thousand ninety six by default, one thousand twenty four reserved for the primary instance, and an absolute ceiling of one shifted by the minor number width.

Disabled control character is the null byte. Control characters and input, output, control and local mode flags are all read through per TTY selectors over the active termios, covering interrupt, quit, erase, kill, end of file, timing, minimum, switch, start, stop, suspend, end of line pair, reprint, discard, word erase and literal next characters plus the standard mode bits.

TTY object combines reference counting, index, device and driver links, port link and operations table with discipline pointer and semaphore, several mutexes and semaphores for atomic writes, legacy handling, throttling, termios and window size, dual termios images, name, flags, open count, receive room and window size. Flow state and session plus packet state live in small locked subgroups, followed by hardware stop, closing and flow change markers, peer link, async notification, read write and break waits, hangup work, discipline and driver private pointers, file list lock with write accounting and buffer, file list and deferred secure attention work. The type carries __randomize_layout.
Per open private record links the TTY object, the open file and list linkage for the owning TTY file set.

Flag word tracks throttling, I/O failure, peer closure, exclusivity, write wakeup demand, discipline presence, PTY locking, write split suppression, hangup completion and progress, plus discipline replacement and halt. Nonblocking input is reported when the file requests it or replacement is underway; I/O failure mirrors its dedicated bit.

Minimal configuration replaces process group, hangup, controlling terminal, device number, process cleanup, current TTY, initialization, naming, privileged open, close and name to number helpers with constant null, zero or standard error results.
Reference helper safely tolerates a null argument and otherwise acquires a strong reference before returning the same pointer.

Transmit helpers and the shared pump dereference the port parent state and its embedded queue without local validity checks, so callers must stabilize port and state lifetime and hold the port lock across use; transmitting while detached or concurrently freed risks invalid access.
